problem: LLMs are promising for zero-shot language-driven robot interaction, but it is unclear how well they handle navigation and exploration with ambiguous or incomplete visual input, and where they fail when controlling real robot platforms.
motivation: HRI needs robots that follow natural language commands without task-specific training. Understanding the strengths and failure modes of LLMs as zero-shot controllers is needed before real-world deployment.
key_idea: Empirically probe LLMs as zero-shot navigation/exploration controllers for PR2 and Khepera IV robots in simulation, and characterize their capabilities (exploratory behavior, iterative reasoning) and failures.
insight: From the abstract only: LLMs show exploratory behavior and iterative reasoning under ambiguous or incomplete visual input. They also show target-recognition errors, object misidentification, hallucination and movement-execution problems. No ablations are described in the abstract.
method: Zero-shot LLM controller: an LLM is prompted, without task-specific training, to perform navigation and exploration from natural language commands and visual input.
Robot platforms: evaluated on the PR2 (Clearpath) and Khepera IV robots.
Simulated environment: experiments run in simulation, with qualitative analysis of behaviors and failure modes.

setting.observation: visual input (details not given in abstract)
setting.action_space: robot movement commands (details not given in abstract)

results: The study reports qualitatively promising results: LLMs exhibit exploratory behavior and iterative reasoning under ambiguous visual input. Failures include target recognition, object misidentification, hallucination and movement execution. No quantitative results appear in the abstract.
limitations: Simulation only; real-world applicability is unverified.
Failures in target recognition, object misidentification, hallucination and movement execution.
